message: Operation 'findEmail' has semantic quality issues: vague_summary, missing_input_details, missing_context. Original summary 'Find a work email address' is too generic and doesn't clarify the required inputs (name and domain). Description is comprehensive but lacks clear input parameter documentation and early stopping conditions are buried in the text. Improved summary specifies the method (from name and domain). Enhanced description reorganizes information to clearly state required inputs upfront, explains the search algorithm and stopping conditions more explicitly, clarifies the billing impact (each format counts as a verification), and explicitly lists key response fields for AI agent interpretability.

data.current_description: Tests the most common address formats for a person at a company domain, one by one and in order of frequency (first.last, flast, first, firstlast, first_last, f.last), and returns the first one the mail server accepts. Names are normalised the way mail servers expect them: lowercase, accents removed (ä, ö, ü become ae, oe, ue), hyphens kept, spaces and apostrophes removed. The search stops as soon as an address is accepted, or on a verdict that applies to the whole domain (Catch-All, No MX, Disposable, SPAM Block, Greylisted, Timeout, MX Error) or to the person (Limited: the mailbox exists but cannot receive). Each format tested counts as one verification, reported in `permutations` and listed in `tested`. `format` gives the pattern found and `confidence` how sure the address is to belong to the person. Paid keys only. A search usually takes one to a few seconds; allow up to 45 seconds.
data.summary_suggestion: Find a person's work email from name and domain
data.description_suggestion: Searches for a person's work email address at a company domain by testing common address formats (first.last, flast, first, firstlast, first_last, f.last) in order of frequency. Requires first name, last name, and domain as inputs. Names are normalized (lowercase, accents removed, spaces/apostrophes removed). Returns the first accepted address with a confidence score, or stops early on domain-level verdicts (Catch-All, No MX, Disposable, SPAM Block, Greylisted, Timeout, MX Error) or person-level verdicts (Limited). Each format tested counts toward daily verification limits. Paid keys only. Typically completes in 1-45 seconds. Response includes `format` (matched pattern), `confidence` (certainty score), `tested` (formats attempted), and `permutations` (count of formats tested).
